findings.summary: The canonical JSON packet has the assigned byte hash, but its reviewed-input identity no longer binds the current target bytes.
evidence: The packet records target content SHA-256 `9d07fac41a1ca773ab4b9bd44d8fa7d3de1a6f23d798d23539c71f6819446847`.
Both packet and target are currently untracked, so no repository commit binds the reviewed bytes independently.
findings.action: After the design repairs, regenerate the canonical JSON packet from the final target and rerun the bounded review against the new packet and reviewed-input identities.

counterweight_triage.disposition: Strong. The decision claims a complete 46-to-13+1 qualification but preserves only the selected cohort; the cited tracker artifact covers a different 16-issue sweep, and the planned spec freezes only 14 selected rows. Bind the full inclusion/exclusion matrix, or narrow the success claim to an explicitly non-exhaustive cohort, before spec.

Strong. Lines 17-23 say issue retirement and worker capability are independent, but dependency step 4 makes write-capable lanes precede the remaining issue workstreams. Give both tracks independent terminal criteria and require an explicit causal edge before any issue row depends on lane adoption.

Strong but cheap to repair. The artifact correctly labels relative-path failure as an unreproduced hypothesis and Q4 as an implementation probe, while dependency step 3 unconditionally says to repair it. Make reproduction the gate and remove repair work if root-cwd and unrelated-cwd controls refute the hypothesis.

Mistaken premise. The reviewer hashed the human Markdown rendering; the assigned identity belongs to the canonical JSON packet, whose SHA-256 is exactly `10eb42f128451efaef600c594da3be7cb31f281f1959cd0b7bc08b8dbacb0bd9`. Its remaining semantic findings remain independently triageable.

Strong and reinforced by II-1. A durable invocation entity needs a minimum operator lifecycle, not merely a command name: durable ID, inspect/status, identity-bound terminal collection, parent-loss or timeout recovery, and non-overwriting repeated collection. Decide whether this extends `charness task` or uses a distinct surface before spec.

Real, but managed local-instruction wiring is assigned to the later write-capable lane layer. The first read-only capability can bind tracked instructions and structured authority without promising portable `AGENTS.local.md` composition; tracked inclusion, precedence, collision recovery, and git-clean proof belong to that later slice.

Real and first-slice relevant, but specifiable within the read-only slice. The target already separates tracked defaults, ignored structured grants, and prose policy. The slice must add deterministic precedence, explicit no-silent-fallback/escalation behavior, preflight visibility, and requested-versus-effective authority in the receipt.

Real for timeout and failed-run recovery, which the first read-only slice can prove with one terminal receipt, preserved logs, idempotent collection, and explicit retry identity. Partial write-worktree preparation, rollback, and destructive cleanup confirmation may remain scoped to the later write-capable slice.

Strong but already aligned with the named installed-consumer slice and truth tests. Make that acceptance concrete by installing the real distributable with the source checkout inaccessible, discovering the CLI from installed help, resolving every exported helper/schema, running and collecting one read-only worker, and rejecting authoring-tree path leakage.

Strong. `charness task` already owns `.charness/tasks/*.json` plus claim, submit, abort, status, artifacts, and persisted recovery affordances. The design proposes another durable entity without dispositioning that owner. Choose extension/composition or an explicit migration and distinct responsibility before naming a lane store.

Strong. The repository currently has independently owned Python reviewer and JavaScript Codex-eval argv/env/auth normalization plus separate reviewer-adapter and capability-local settings. Choosing only to 'extract or reuse' risks a third owner. Name the canonical executable boundary and field-level configuration ownership/migration before spec.

Strong and executable within the read-only slice. The current runtime validates identities repeated by the result but does not re-observe a general subject manifest. Assign pre-launch and post-collection hashing to the process boundary and prove subject, instruction, policy, or checkout drift yields `input-drift`, never delivery.

Strong. Dependency step 3 makes the repaired proof surface perform the task-completing review used to dogfood itself. The north star requires a different observer and evidence channel, and the operating contract adds a second bounded round after verdict-logic repairs. Reserve a pre-existing independent review channel for acceptance and treat candidate-command dogfood only as supplementary behavior evidence.

next_move: Keep Option B provisional, but before spec: bind an auditable issue cohort; separate issue retirement from lane adoption and make the path repair reproduction-conditional; choose `charness task` extension versus a distinct migrated durable owner; name one canonical process/configuration authority; define the minimum durable operator lifecycle; and reserve an independent acceptance channel for proof-surface changes. Then regenerate the JSON packet from the repaired target and rerun bounded review. Backend precedence, timeout recovery, installed-package proof, and executable input-drift observation can be completed in the first read-only slice; local-instruction and write-worktree recovery remain deferred to the write-capable slice.
non_claims: No files, git state, GitHub state, or Ceal state were modified.
No live GitHub cohort refresh was performed, so no claim is made that the listed 13+1 cohort is substantively complete or incomplete.
No backend worker, installed-package acceptance run, broad quality gate, or write-capable worktree test was executed.
This review does not reject Option B or require write-capable lanes in the first slice.
OPR-001 is rejected only for hashing the wrong packet representation; its semantic sibling findings were independently evaluated.
Because the current target bytes differ from the packet-bound bytes, this verdict is not an approval of either byte version and must not be used as approval-eligible closeout evidence.
